coverageDimensions: REGION: rich. The page names 38 Regions explicitly, in prose form, as its section structure, and asserts a per-Region rule list for each. This is the page's real second dimension. It does NOT give region codes, does not name partitions, does not say a Region is unsupported, and does not claim the 38 are all AWS Regions - Regions absent from this page (for example any Region with no managed rules documented here) are simply not mentioned. SERVICE: nothing stated. Rule names contain service-ish prefixes (s3-, ec2-, iam-, sagemaker-, amplify-), but the page never declares a service column, never names a service, and prefixes are unreliable - api-gw-, api-gwv2- and apigatewayv2- are three prefixes for the same service, and rules like access-keys-rotated or account-part-of-organizations carry no prefix at all. Any per-service count from this page is fabricated. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing stated. The page never names an AWS::*::* resource type or any evaluated resource. A rule's target resource type lives on the linked per-rule page, not here. Any resource-type figure attributed to this page is fabricated.

features.collapse: The page's rows are (rule, Region) pairs, not rules. The same rule name is repeated once in every Region where it is available, so access-keys-rotated alone contributes dozens of bullets. 21,391 bullets across the 38 Region lists name only 822 distinct managed rule identifiers. Per-Region bullet counts range from 204 (Asia Pacific (Taipei)) to 814 (US East (N. Virginia)); no single Region list is the full catalogue, so the 822 union is larger than any one Region's count. Within any one Region list every rule name is unique - the duplication is purely across Regions.
features.featureName: AWS Config managed rules by Region availability
features.reasoning: The unit AWS is actually asserting is 'rule X is available in Region Y', so the enumerated thing is the managed rule and the Region is the scope. configRule is the correct axis name: these are AWS Config managed rules, a catalogue AWS publishes about its own service, identified by hyphenated ids like s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited. The axis is catalogue, not external, because the values exist only because AWS Config defines them. I set expectedCount to the 21,391 bullet rows because that is what a parser walking this page will encounter, and distinctTargets to the 822 unique rule ids because that is the size of the catalogue the rows name. Treating the Region as the axis instead would be wrong: the Regions are section headings, and a Region-axis reading would throw away the entire body of the page and reduce a 21,391-assertion matrix to the number 38.
features.scope: Per-Region, and that is the whole point of the page. The second dimension has 38 values: US East (Ohio), US East (N. Virginia), US West (N. California), US West (Oregon), Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Hong Kong), Asia Pacific (Hyderabad), Asia Pacific (Jakarta), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Melbourne), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Asia Pacific (Osaka), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Taipei), Asia Pacific (Thailand), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), Canada West (Calgary), China (Beijing), China (Ningxia), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Milan), Europe (Paris), Europe (Spain), Europe (Stockholm), Europe (Zurich), Israel (Tel Aviv), Mexico (Central), Middle East (Bahrain), Middle East (UAE), South America (Sao Paulo), AWS GovCloud (US-East), AWS GovCloud (US-West). Regions are named in prose form only - the page never prints an API region code such as us-east-2, so any code mapping is inference, not something the page states. The list spans three partitions (aws, aws-cn, aws-us-gov) but the page never uses the word partition.
features.statuses: 21391 Yes, 0 No, 0 Partial; 21391+0+0=21391. Every bullet is a bare link to a rule page, which I read as 'this managed rule is available in this Region'. The page contains no negative marker anywhere - no 'No' cell, no 'not available', no exclusion note, no strikethrough, no asterisk. The 38 x 822 = 31,236 possible (rule, Region) cells minus the 21,391 stated ones leaves 9,845 cells the page is simply SILENT about. Those 9,845 are absence, not a stated No, and must not be scored as negative coverage.
features.waived: The reading is correct and we do not dispute it: the page states 21,391 rule-by-Region facts over 822 rules. We do not publish them. A claim per rule per Region is a claim about 822 individual rules, and stating it honestly needs a row per rule. Instead the catalogue is counted (822 rules published) and the Region scope is measured (38 Regions, each carrying how many rules are available there), which is the same page read at the granularity of the feature that owns it.

pageTitle: List of AWS Config Managed Rules by Region Availability
shouldNotExtract: The 'See also' H2 and its single bullet about AWS Agent Toolkit skills is boilerplate, not coverage - it is an H2 sitting at the same level as the 38 Region sections and will be counted as a 39th Region by any parser that just counts H2s. The intro sentence and its link to Considerations (evaluate-config.md#evaluate-config-considerations) is a cross-reference, not a rule. The 77 HTML anchor tags (one '<a name=...-section-head>' per H2 plus one '<a name=...>' per H3, plus the page-level anchor) are navigation. The doubled headings are the same Region twice, not two Regions. The .html hrefs on each bullet point at per-rule reference pages elsewhere in the guide and are not themselves coverage values. Nothing on this page is a quota, a limit, a parameter, a severity, or a resource type.
trap: The single most likely misparse is deduplicating the bullets and reporting 822 as the page's coverage number, silently discarding the Region dimension that the page exists to express - or the mirror-image error of reporting 21,391 as if AWS Config had 21,391 distinct managed rules. Both numbers are real; they answer different questions and neither alone describes the page. Runners-up: (1) counting H2 headings and getting 39 Regions because 'See also' is an H2; (2) counting H2 plus H3 and getting 76 Region sections because every Region is titled twice; (3) treating the 9,845 unstated (rule, Region) cells as explicit 'No' and reporting negative coverage the page never asserts; (4) reading a Region's list length as the AWS Config rule catalogue size - US East (N. Virginia) has 814 of the 822, so a single-Region parse looks almost right and is still wrong; (5) inferring per-service coverage from rule-name prefixes; (6) mangling 'South America (Sao Paulo)' on the non-ASCII character or splitting Region names on the internal parentheses.
whatThePageStates: The page is a single sentence of intro followed by 38 region sections, one per AWS Region. Each region gets an H2 named '<Region> Region' and an identical H3 named '<Region>', under which a flat bullet list links every AWS Config managed rule that is available in that Region. There is no table, no Yes/No column, no legend and no footnote: availability is asserted only by a rule appearing in a Region's list. Across the 38 Regions there are 21,391 rule bullets naming 822 distinct managed rules. The only other content is a trailing 'See also' section of AI-coding-assistant boilerplate.
